cat >> /home/lane/MythosMini/journal.md <<'EOF'

## [2026-06-12 11:30] — double-decoder math experiment: diffusion thinker + AR talker beats size-matched AR baseline in low-budget regime

**TL;DR:** Built the user's double-decoder idea as a tiny math test model in tests/ (tests/double_decoder.py, commit f864821): a bidirectional discrete-diffusion "thinker" generates a 7-char column-sum/carry scratchpad for 3-digit addition, then a causal AR "talker" emits the 4-digit answer conditioned on it; compared against a depth-matched single AR baseline (~137k vs ~140k params). At low training budgets the double decoder wins decisively (steps=150: 13–32% vs 1–5%; steps=300: 90–99% vs 20–92%); at full budget (1200 steps) the baseline saturates at 100% while the double decoder caps at 98.8%. The talker given ground-truth thoughts scores 100% everywhere — all residual error is the thinker's. Best-of-8 candidate ranking by talker log-prob is consistently WORSE than a single greedy thought. 13 new tests pass.

**Long description:** Task per user: prompt `abc+def=`, engineered two-response dataset per prompt — quick-thinking response (right-to-left per-column digit+carry string, 7 chars, produced by render_example) and polished answer (`%04d`). Thinker = 2-layer bidirectional transformer trained with masked-denoising (mask ratio U(0.2,1.0), CE on masked think positions; diffusion_training_loss), inference = 6-step confidence-scheduled iterative unmasking (diffusion_sample). Talker = 2-layer causal transformer on [prompt;SEP;think;SEP;answer], CE on answer tokens. Baseline = 4-layer causal AR on [prompt;SEP;answer] to match total depth/params. d=64, h=4, ffn=128, batch 256, AdamW 3e-3, 30k train / 500 held-out test examples. Best-of-K variant: 8 temperature-1.0 sampled thoughts, greedy talker answer per thought, winner by talker mean log-prob. run_experiment drives everything; e2e test runs a shrunk full pipeline. Full-budget run (1200 steps): baseline 1.000, double greedy 0.988, best-of-8 0.938, oracle-thought 1.000, 57.1 s wall on CPU. Budget sweep (2 seeds each): steps=150 baseline 0.008/0.054 vs double 0.134/0.320; steps=300 baseline 0.204/0.916 vs double 0.896/0.988; steps=600 baseline 0.998/1.000 vs double 0.934/0.990. Best-of-8 below greedy at every point (e.g. 0.750 vs 0.896 at 300 steps).

**What worked:** The user's core hypothesis — two small decoders specializing in complementary work learn the task far faster than one network doing everything — reproduced cleanly: the decomposition moves the hard carry computation into a parallel bidirectional denoiser and leaves the talker a near-copy task (oracle accuracy 1.0 after a few hundred steps). Proving tests written first per sandbox rule: tests/test_double_decoder.py (12 tests: render format incl. carry chain 583+417 -> think "0101011", dataset consistency, loss decrease for all three objectives, full unmasking, greedy determinism, causal mask blocks future, finite losses, exact_match). E2E tests/e2e/test_double_decoder_e2e.py runs run_experiment end to end on CPU. 13/13 passed in 3.17 s. make lint exit 0, make pyaot "checked 83 file(s) — 0 error(s)".

**What failed:** (1) First diffusion_sample left MASK_ID tokens forever: an untrained sampler can draw MASK_ID itself, so the position never counts as revealed — verbatim test failure "assert not tensor(True) ... thinks == MASK_ID". Fixed by banning ids 0-2 (logits[:, :, :3] = -inf) plus a final argmax fill of leftovers. (2) exact_match test compared float32 mean to exact 2/3 — replaced with 1e-6 tolerance. (3) Running on GPU failed immediately: "torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory" — the GPU is ~99% occupied by other processes the user said not to kill; experiment ran on CPU instead (57 s, well within budget). tests/test_hardware.py::test_detect_device_returns_consistent_info also failed once with the same CUDA OOM (known transient contention mode, see 2026-06-10 12:10 entry); full suite re-run with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="". (4) Negative finding on the user's variant 2: ranking 8 sampled thoughts by the talker's own answer log-prob is anti-helpful at this scale (best-of-8 lost to single greedy at every budget) — the talker is confidently fluent on wrong scratchpads, so likelihood is not a usable verifier signal here. Do not retry log-prob ranking unchanged; a trained verifier head or answer-consistency voting would be the next thing to try.

**What was kept / discarded:** Kept tests/double_decoder.py, both test files, docs/functions.md entries for all 16 new functions (commit f864821). Discarded nothing; the sampling fix replaced the broken first draft before commit.

**Open questions / next steps:** (1) The crossover (baseline catches up by ~600 steps) suggests the decomposition advantage is a sample/compute-efficiency effect, not a capacity ceiling — testing at harder tasks (5+ digit addition, multiplication) where the baseline may never converge is the natural follow-up. (2) Thinker is the sole error source; more diffusion steps or a larger thinker / smaller talker split is untested. (3) Candidate selection needs a real verifier signal (see negative finding). (4) Full make test on CPU was still running at entry time; result recorded in the next entry.
EOF
git add journal.md && git commit -q -m "journal double-decoder experiment results" && git log --oneline -1
